name: k6
tagline: Scripted load tests with pass/fail thresholds, gating releases on p95.

howItWorks.title: Scenarios and VUs
howItWorks.body:
A scenario picks an executor, load shape and duration.
ramping-vus changes concurrent virtual users over stages.
constant-arrival-rate holds requests per second regardless of response time.
Several scenarios run in parallel to mix traffic.

howItWorks.title: Thresholds
howItWorks.body:
Thresholds are pass or fail rules on metrics, such as http_req_duration p(95)<500.
http_req_failed rate<0.01 caps errors at one percent.
Tags scope a threshold to one request name.
Any failure makes k6 exit with code 99.

howItWorks.title: Metrics and remote write
howItWorks.body:
k6 records http_req_duration, http_reqs and dropped_iterations for every run.
The experimental-prometheus-rw output pushes them to Prometheus.
Prometheus needs --web.enable-remote-write-receiver enabled.
TREND_STATS turns trends into series like k6_http_req_duration_p95.

howItWorks.title: Grafana dashboard
howItWorks.body:
Grafana reads the k6_ series from the Prometheus data source.
Panels show p95 latency, requests per second and error rate.
A testid variable separates one run from another.

howItWorks.title: Load test before release
howItWorks.body:
The pipeline runs k6 as a gate after deploy to staging.
A failed threshold fails the stage and blocks promotion.
Compare p95 against the previous release in Grafana.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
A CI stage or an engineer starts k6 with a script and an environment-supplied base URL.
The k6 exit code fails the build when a threshold breaks.
The k6 Operator can run distributed tests on Kubernetes.
Keep the load generator off the target nodes.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Virtual users hit the real entry path: load balancer, gateway, then the Service.
Tokens come from the identity provider in setup(), then are reused.
Results flow out by Prometheus remote write, or other outputs such as InfluxDB or OpenTelemetry.
Grafana plots them beside server-side metrics (Platform).

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
JMeter: GUI and plugin ecosystem; choose it for protocol breadth.
Locust: load scripts written in Python.
Gatling: Scala or Java DSL with rich reports.
Vegeta or wrk: choose them for a quick single-endpoint rate test.

flow: Pipeline starts k6 with a script and a testid tag.
Scenario ramps virtual users or holds an arrival rate.
Each VU sends requests to the target through the gateway.
k6 records http_req_duration for every request.
Thresholds are evaluated continuously during the run.
Metrics are pushed to Prometheus by remote write.
Grafana plots p95, throughput and errors per testid.

deploy.summary: Run k6 on a Linux VM with Docker against a target, ship metrics to Prometheus, chart in Grafana.
prerequisites: Grafana with the Prometheus data source

steps.title: Allow the load generator through the firewall
steps.code:
# on the Prometheus host: accept remote write from the k6 VM (placeholder IP)
sudo ufw allow from 192.0.2.20 to any port 9090 proto tcp
# Prometheus must run with: --web.enable-remote-write-receiver
steps.note: Without the flag Prometheus answers 404 on /api/v1/write.

steps.title: Test script with scenario and thresholds
steps.note: Save as script.js. Set TARGET to your service.

steps.title: Run it with pinned k6
steps.code:
docker run --rm -i --network host -e TARGET=http://localhost:8081 grafana/k6:0.52.0 run - < script.js
echo "exit code: $?"
steps.note: Exit 0 means thresholds passed; 99 means one failed.

steps.title: Constant arrival rate scenario
steps.note: Replace the options block to hold 100 requests per second.

steps.title: Remote write to Prometheus
steps.code:
docker run --rm -i --network host \
  -e TARGET=http://localhost:8081 \
  -e K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/write \
  -e K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS='p(95),p(99),avg,max' \
  grafana/k6:0.52.0 run -o experimental-prometheus-rw --tag testid=release-001 - < script.js
steps.note: Use the Prometheus host address when it is not local.

steps.title: Grafana dashboard provisioning
steps.note: Save as /var/lib/grafana/dashboards/k6.json. Provide it with a file provider in /etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/k6.yaml, then restart Grafana.

steps.title: Nightly run as a systemd unit
steps.code:
[Unit]
Description=Nightly k6 load test
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
Environment=K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/write
Environment=K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS=p(95),p(99),avg,max
ExecStart=/usr/bin/k6 run -o experimental-prometheus-rw --tag testid=nightly /opt/k6/script.js
steps.note: Save as /etc/systemd/system/k6-nightly.service, add a timer, then systemctl daemon-reload. Needs k6 installed from the k6 package.

steps.title: Gate a release in Jenkins
steps.note: A threshold failure returns exit 99 and fails the stage.

verify: Thresholds: k6 exit code 0 after run (echo $?)
Dashboard loads: Grafana > Dashboards > k6 load test, set testid
pitfalls: Load generator saturates its own CPU and reports false latency; watch it.
Closed models with VUs hide overload; use constant-arrival-rate for throughput targets.
Testing through a CDN or cache measures the cache, not your service.
Forgetting the remote-write receiver flag gives 404 and no series.
Unscoped thresholds average away a slow endpoint; tag requests and scope them.
Think time missing from the script makes unrealistic traffic; add sleep().
Output names and metric naming change by version; pin k6 and check docs.
keyPoints: Scenarios define who arrives: VUs ramping, or a constant arrival rate.
Thresholds turn p95 and error rate into a pass or fail.
Metrics stream to Prometheus by remote write for Grafana.
Run the test before release; a failed threshold blocks it.
quickDeploy: Install k6 or pull the pinned Docker image.
Write a script with a scenario and thresholds.
Run it with Prometheus remote write output.
Wire it into the pipeline before release.
osiNote: Generates HTTP, gRPC and WebSocket load at the application layer.
production: Test a production-like environment, never a shared dev box.
Run load generators on separate VMs from the target.
Use constant-arrival-rate to hold throughput when latency rises.
Tag every run with testid and compare against the last release.
Alert on dropped_iterations; the generator itself may be the limit.
